subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What do the interior angles of a triangle add up to?
questions.explain: The interior angles of any triangle always sum to 180°.

questions.q: Angles meeting at a point on a straight line add up to how many degrees?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line form a half-turn, summing to 180°.

questions.q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular pentagon?
questions.explain: The interior angles sum to (5−2)×180° = 540°, so each is 540°÷5 = 108°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon?
options: depends on the number of sides
questions.explain: The exterior angles of any convex polygon always add up to 360°.

questions.q: What do the interior angles of a quadrilateral add up to?
questions.explain: A quadrilateral splits into two triangles, so its angles sum to 2×180° = 360°.

questions.q: Which formula gives the area of a circle of radius r?
questions.explain: The area of a circle is π multiplied by the radius squared.

questions.q: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle of radius r?
questions.explain: The circumference equals 2πr (equivalently πd, where d is the diameter).

questions.q: How is the volume of a cuboid calculated?
questions.explain: The volume of a cuboid is the product of its three dimensions.

questions.q: A triangle has a base of 8 cm and a perpendicular height of 5 cm. What is its area?
questions.explain: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm².

questions.q: Which formula gives the volume of a cylinder with radius r and height h?
questions.explain: The volume of a cylinder is the circular cross-sectional area (πr²) multiplied by the height.

questions.q: A circle has a radius of 3 cm. Using π ≈ 3.14, what is its area (to 1 d.p.)?
questions.explain: Area = πr² = 3.14 × 3² = 28.3 cm² to 1 decimal place.

questions.q: Pythagoras' theorem for a right-angled triangle states that:
questions.explain: The square of the hypotenuse (c) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs of 5 cm and 12 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
In a right-angled triangle, the sine of an angle is defined as:
questions.explain: Sine is the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse (SOH).

questions.q: Which ratio correctly represents the tangent of an angle in a right-angled triangle?
questions.explain: Tangent is the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side (TOA).

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs of 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
To fully describe a rotation, which three pieces of information are required?
questions.explain: A rotation is defined by its centre, the angle of turn and the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise).

questions.q: A shape is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. By what factor does its area increase?
questions.explain: Area scales by the square of the length scale factor, so 3² = 9.

questions.q: How is a translation of a shape described?
questions.explain: A translation is described by a column vector giving the horizontal and vertical movement.

questions.q: Which statement is true about a reflection?
options: It changes the size of the shape
The image is congruent to the object
It requires a centre and angle
It is described by a column vector
questions.explain: Reflection produces a mirror image that is the same size and shape, so it is congruent.

questions.q: How is a bearing correctly measured and written?
questions.explain: Bearings are measured clockwise from north and always written using three figures.

questions.q: An angle in a semicircle, drawn from the ends of the diameter to a point on the circumference, is always:
questions.explain: The angle subtended in a semicircle (angle in a semicircle theorem) is a right angle, 90°.

questions.q: The bearing of B from A is 070°. What is the bearing of A from B?
questions.explain: The back bearing is found by adding 180° to a bearing under 180°, giving 070° + 180° = 250°.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Mathematics (2017) specification; Geometry & Measures
